entities.summary: Oluwa Forest Reserve is located in Ondo State, Nigeria and covers over 829 km2 (320 sq mi). It is part of the Omo, Shasha and Oluwa forest reserves, although it has become separated from the Omo and Shasha reserves. The three reserves contain some of the last remaining forest in the area. Although they are biologically unique, they are threatened by logging, hunting and agriculture. The natural vegetation of the area is tropical rainforest. However, the natural vegetation of the area except for the areas devoted to forest reserve has now been reduced to secondary regrowth forest and fallow regrowth at varying stages of development or replaced by perennial and annual crops.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Oluwa Forest Reserve's loss of natural vegetation due to logging and agriculture has significant regional implications for biodiversity conservation in West Africa. The reserve's unique ecosystem supports a range of endemic species found nowhere else.
